docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Legendary FFXI Private Server

Private Server

Extreme QoL. Fast progression. No grind tax.

Hit 99 in an hour. Chase best-in-slot for months. This is FFXI the way it should feel.

Legendary is a private FFXI server built around one idea: the grind should be fun, not a wall. We cut the mandatory busywork, kept the depth, and bolted on a custom endgame that gives you something real to chase — whether you've been playing for a week or a year.

New Player? Start here.

Don't know where to begin? The Getting Started guide walks you through installing the client, connecting to the server, and taking your first steps — in about 20 minutes.

docs.title: What makes Legendary different
docs.text:
Retail FFXI is a masterpiece buried under 20 years of time-gating. Most private servers swing the other direction and trivialize everything. Legendary splits the difference:

  • Fast leveling, real endgame. 3× mob EXP (plus 10× from books, FoV/GoV & Records of Eminence) gets you to 99 in a few hours, not months. Then the actual game begins.
  • Everything unlocked at creation. Advanced jobs, all outpost warps, all maps, full inventory — no arbitrary gates.
  • Custom content built for long-term play. The Hunting League, Dungeon system, Reforge gear, and weekly objectives give you a loop that doesn't expire.
  • A small, friendly community. No drama, no gatekeeping — just people who like this game.

docs.title: Feature highlights
docs.text:
Hunting League — A custom 5-rank NM hunting system. Kill your way from Initiate to Legend, unlocking gear, titles, and HL Points at every tier.

Ascension — The endgame above the endgame. Reaching Legend opens a per-job, no-cap progression track: re-clear escalating superboss Courts to bank Ascension Points and spend them on permanent stat boosts. The gauntlet swaps to a deadlier roster every 10 ascensions, so the climb never goes stale.

Dungeons — Four dungeons with Normal, Hard, and Mythic difficulties. Random affixes, streak multipliers, and the rarest gear drops in the game.

Reforge system — Three parallel NM ladders (AF, Relic, Empy) that upgrade your armor from base all the way to +3. Best-in-slot is earnable, not bought.

Augment Moogle — 400+ augment options. Trade catalysts from NM kills to permanently customize your gear in ways retail never allowed.

Weekly Hunt Board — Five rotating objectives every week. Complete all five for a big bonus. Always something to do.

Wave Master — An NPC arena in Escha - Ru'Aun that spawns themed NM waves for solo or group practice. Earn Hunt Marks. Flex on your friends.

Hunter's Guild — Four hunting guilds that rank up as you kill their NMs, permanently boosting the marks every kill pays out. Hit Grandmaster across all of them for the Trinity and Apex Hunter titles.

Custom Trusts — Allies you won't find on retail: Gemma (a full healer / buffer / debuffer in a deceptively small package) and Meat (an unkillable wall that never drops aggro).

Living economy — The auction house is never empty: a market-maker keeps thousands of gear listings stocked around the clock — a built-in price floor and gil sink — so you can actually buy your upgrades.

Achievements & Leaderboards — 26 milestones that pay bonus marks and titles as you rack up first kills, tier climbs, and lifetime records — plus live server leaderboards (top hunters, fastest clears, most augments) to climb.

docs.text:

These docs track the live server

Legendary is under active development, and the developer makes every effort to keep this site in step with it. Many pages — server rates, player commands, spell lists, gear, Hunting League tiers, augment values — are generated straight from the live server's own data and refreshed regularly, so what you read here reflects what's actually running in-game. The hand-written guides are revised alongside every mechanics and custom-content change. Spot something that's drifted out of date? Flag it on Discord and it'll be fixed.

docs.title: New character bonuses
docs.text:
Every new character starts with:

  • 5,000,000 Gil in your wallet
  • 80 inventory slots (the maximum)
  • All maps for every zone
  • All outpost warps already unlocked
  • Advanced jobs unlocked — no quest required
  • Subjob unlocked — use it at full level immediately

docs.title: What's waiting at endgame?
docs.text:
The real game starts at 99.

Most servers have nothing to do after you level cap. Legendary was built around this problem.

Hunting League (5 tiers) Progress through Initiate → Hunter → Elite → Champion → Legend by killing increasingly difficult NMs. Each tier unlocks stronger gear options, higher HL Point rates, and exclusive titles. The grind is real — and it's meant to be.

Ascension / Prestige (the layer above Legend) The true ceiling. Reaching Legend tier opens the Ascension Altar in Provenance — a per-job, infinite progression track. Defeat the Nightmare Court (three dread superbosses), pay an escalating Mark cost, and bank Ascension Points to permanently empower the job you're playing. And the deeper you ascend, the harder the NMs hit back — difficulty climbs in tiers as your prestige grows, so the challenge always keeps pace with your power.

Hunter's Guild (4 guilds, lifetime amplifiers) A passive reputation layer on top of every NM track. Each guild — AF, Relic, Empyrean, and League — ranks up as you kill its NMs, permanently amplifying the marks you earn from that source. Push to Grandmaster across multiple guilds for the Trinity and Apex Hunter capstones. The more you hunt, the more every kill pays out.

Dungeon System (4 dungeons, 3 difficulties) Four dungeons, each with Normal, Hard, and Mythic clears. Mythic is gated behind five Hard clears and a weekly key. Random affixes mean every run plays differently. The best gear in the game drops here.

Reforge Gear (+3 from NM kills) Three independent NM ladders — AF Marks from Sky Gods, Relic Marks from Unity NMs, Empy Marks from Abyssea NMs — each upgrades a full armor set from base to +1 to +2 to +3. No RNG. No gatcha. Just kills.

Augment Moogle (400+ augment options) Catalysts drop from monsters across the world. Trade them to the Augment Moogle to permanently apply stat bonuses to your gear. Pair with the Augment Sage — an NPC whose bonuses scale with your NM kill history — to push augment strength even further.

Weekly Hunt Board Five objectives, reset every week. Ranging from "kill 10 of X" to "clear a Mythic dungeon." Complete all five and you earn a significant bonus. Always rotating, never stale.

Daily Board Three fresh objectives every day, reset at UTC midnight — drawn from five metric groups (kills, dungeons, infamy, wave fights, augments), so it never plays out the same way twice. Clear all three in one day for a bonus on top. The daily counterpart to the Weekly Hunt Board.

Wave Master Head to Escha - Ru'Aun and talk to the Wave Master NPC to start a themed NM wave event — solo or with a group. Scales with your party. Earns Hunt Marks. Good for practice, great for marks farming.

Custom Trusts Summons you won't find on retail. Gemma is a premium support Trust: a tiny Hume woman who heals, raises, buffs, debuffs, sings, rolls, and magic-bursts your skillchains without ever pulling hate. Meat is an unkillable tank Trust that soaks every hit and refuses to let go of aggro. Both are permanent 50M-gil unlocks — a serious late-game gil sink.

Achievements (26 milestones) Twenty-six personal milestones — first kills, tier climbs, lifetime mark totals, dungeon clears, and Infamy hauls — each paying bonus Hunt Marks, with the biggest ones awarding a title and a server-wide announcement. Side-goals that tick along under everything else you do.

Leaderboards See where you rank across the server — most augments crafted, top hunters, fastest clears, and more — pulled live from the database and refreshed a few times a day. Chase the top spot, or opt any character out if you'd rather hunt in peace.

Think this sounds good? Get started now. Or read What's Custom for the full breakdown of every change.

docs.title: Server Rules
docs.text: Legendary is a small, friendly community. We have a short list of rules designed to keep it that way. None of this is complicated — just be a reasonable person and you'll be fine.

docs.title: The Short Version
docs.text:
• Cheating is frowned upon. Bots, automation, and packet editing are discouraged — play fair.
  • Be decent to people. Harassment isn't tolerated.
  • No real-money trading. Gil and items stay in-game. Period.
  • Don't exploit bugs. Found one? Report it. Don't farm it.
  • No account limits. Multi-box as much as you like.
  • GMs are not vending machines. They don't spawn items or content on request.

docs.title: Fair Play
docs.text:
Cheating is frowned upon. Third-party tools that automate gameplay — combat bots, AHK macros that play the game for you, and anything that removes the need for a human at the keyboard — go against the spirit of the server, and the community tends to look down on them.

Quality-of-life plugins through Windower or Ashita are fine — maps, chat filters, bag sorting, item tooltips. We're not interested in policing the things that make the game more playable.

Speedhacks, wallhacks, and packet editing fall into the same "frowned upon" bucket: they hand you an edge over people playing with just the game client, and that's not the kind of play we want to encourage. If you're unsure whether a tool crosses the line, ask in Discord.

docs.title: Economy
docs.text: No real-money trading. Gil and items exist in the game economy, not for sale outside of it. Selling or buying Gil for real money — or brokering item purchases with real currency — is a permanent ban, no appeal. This isn't about the letter of the rule; it's about keeping the game fair for people who actually play it.

docs.title: Multi-Boxing
docs.text: There are no account limits and no cap on how many characters you run at once. Multi-box freely — a single support character to buff your main, or a full party of your own, it's all fine. Playing multiple characters is a normal part of how a lot of people enjoy FFXI.

docs.title: Bug Reporting
docs.text:
Found a bug or an exploitable mechanic? Report it in the #bugs channel in Discord.

Using an exploit for personal gain before reporting it — especially one that affects the economy, spawn rates, or item acquisition — will result in strikes against your account. How many depends on severity.

Good-faith bug reports are welcomed and rewarded. We'd rather fix something than police it.

docs.title: Community Standards
docs.text:
No harassment, hate speech, slurs, or targeted toxicity. This is a small server — you'll be playing with the same people for months. Act accordingly.

Trash talk in competition is fine. Targeting someone to make them miserable is not. Staff use judgment; there's no exhaustive list of prohibited words.

docs.title: GMs and Staff
docs.text:
GMs are here for server maintenance, not customer service. They do not:

  • Give out items, Gil, or gear
  • Spawn content on demand
  • Intervene in normal competitive gameplay
  • Teleport you because you got stuck (use /heal or rezone)

If you see a GM online, they're doing maintenance. Staff will never ask for your account password or credentials. If someone claiming to be a GM asks for your password, that's an impersonator — report it immediately.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Most rule violations follow a three-strike process:

  1. Warning — you're told what you did and why it's a problem
  2. 24-hour ban — temporary removal from the server
  3. Permanent ban — account terminated

Severe violations — real-money trading, sustained harassment campaigns, large-scale exploiting — skip directly to permanent ban without warning. Staff judgment is final, but bans can be appealed in Discord.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text:
All reports, appeals, and questions go through Discord. Use the appropriate channel:

  • #bugs — bugs and exploits
  • #questions — general questions
  • #recommendations — suggestions and feature ideas
  • #general — everything else: Hall of Fame milestone submissions, and ban appeals or account issues (or DM a GM directly)

The goal is a fun server, not a perfectly policed one. Use good judgment, treat people well, and you'll never have to think about this page again.

docs.title: Why Legendary?
docs.text: Legendary isn't trying to be the biggest FFXI private server. It's trying to be the best one for players who love the game but won't accept the original's worst habits.

docs.title: The Problem with Retail FFXI
docs.text:
Retail is still running, and it's still a remarkable game. But it was designed for a different era:

  • The time investment is brutal. Getting to 99 and gearing a single job for endgame content is a part-time job measured in months — before you've even seen the interesting content.
  • Content is locked behind content. Older endgame systems have been abandoned. The population migrated to Ambuscade, Vagary, and Odyssey. If you want to experience the full sweep of the game's history, you're doing it mostly solo and mostly outdated.
  • The clock is ticking. Square Enix has talked about retail FFXI's future. The private server scene exists precisely because players don't want to lose access to this world.

docs.title: The Problem with Most Private Servers
docs.text:
The private server community is large and passionate, but most servers solve the wrong problem:

  • They make everything too easy. 100× EXP and instant max gear means you've "beaten" the server in a week. There's nothing left to chase, and the population evaporates.
  • There's no custom endgame. Most servers are just retail FFXI with the grind removed. The content cap was never designed to hold players' attention long-term without a reason to keep logging in.
  • The population dies fast. Without a steady content loop, players beat the server, get bored, and leave. You end up playing alone on a ghost server within a month.

docs.title: What Legendary Does Differently
docs.text:
• Fast progression, real endgame. 10× EXP means you hit 99 in an afternoon, not months. But 99 is the beginning, not the finish line. The Hunting League, Dungeon system, Reforge gear, and augments are all designed to hold your interest for months. There's always a next thing.

  • Hunting League — a custom 5-tier progression system. Retail FFXI has NMs. Legendary turns them into a structured progression ladder. Five ranks, each harder than the last, each with meaningful rewards and increasing HL Point rates. If you love the hunt, this server was built for you.

  • Dungeon system — four dungeons, never the same twice. Each dungeon has Normal, Hard, and Mythic difficulty tiers. Mythic is genuinely gated (five Hard clears + a weekly key). Random affixes mean every run is different. The best gear in the game drops in Mythic — and you have to earn it.

  • Reforge system — three NM ladders to +3 BiS. Kill Sky Gods for AF Marks. Kill Unity NMs for Relic Marks. Kill Abyssea NMs for Empy Marks. Each currency line upgrades a full armor set across four tiers. No RNG boxes, no cash shop — just the satisfaction of killing your way to best-in-slot.

  • Augment Moogle — 110+ ways to customize your gear. Catalysts drop from monsters all over the world. Trade them to the Augment Moogle to apply permanent stat bonuses to your gear. Stack them with the Augment Sage (whose power scales with your NM kill history) and you can push gear further than retail ever allowed.

  • No dead content — weekly objectives, daily board, Wave Master arena. The Weekly Hunt Board resets every week with five fresh objectives. The Daily Board resets at midnight UTC. The Wave Master NPC in Balga's Dais spawns NM waves on demand. There is always a reason to log in.

  • Everything unlocked at character creation. No quest to unlock advanced jobs. No tour of outpost warps. No waiting for maps. You create a character and immediately have access to everything that retail made you spend weeks unlocking. The friction that doesn't make the game better is just gone.

Ready to start?

The Getting Started guide will have you in-game in about 20 minutes. Everything else you need is in these docs.

docs.title: What's Custom
docs.text:
Server name: Legendary Tagline: Extreme QoL & Fast Progression

Legendary is a heavily-customized FFXI server. Beyond the settings tweaks (rates, caps, durations), it adds custom NPCs, hunt systems, gear pipelines, and background overrides that don't exist on retail. This page is the index — every custom system is listed here. Detail pages link out for the big content.

docs.title: Subjob
docs.text:
Subjob is full level, not half. If your main is 99, your sub is 99 too. (Retail: sub is half main, so 99/49.)

Subjob also levels itself. While you grind your main, your subjob banks half the EXP and levels up in the background, capped at main's current level. See Subjob EXP Share for the full mechanic.

docs.text:
Higher caps and unlimited spending:

This server Retail Max merit points held 127 30 Sparks cap 999,999 99,999 Accolades cap 999,999 99,999 Valor cap 500,000 50,000 Ballista crystals cap 20,000 2,000 Weekly sparks/accolades spending cap disabled 100,000/week

docs.title: Dynamis
docs.text:
Built for grinding:

  • Cooldown between Dynamis runs: 0h (retail: 24h).
  • Level minimum: 1 (retail: 65).
  • Prismatic Hourglass cost: 1 gil (retail: 50,000).
  • Currency exchange rate: 10:1 (retail: 100:1) — cheaper to upgrade ancient currency.
  • 100s → 1s exchange enabled.
  • COP Dynamis has no Chains of Promathia mission prerequisite (FREE_COP_DYNAMIS = 1).

docs.title: Trusts
docs.text:
• Custom Engagement enabled — trusts behave more flexibly.
  • Alter Ego Extravaganza event running (summer/NY trust acquisition discounts).
  • Alter Ego Expo running (HPP / MPP / Status Resistance bonus).

docs.title: Quality-of-life settings
docs.text:
• @unstuck self-rescue command enabled (24h cooldown).
  • Unlimited AH listings (retail: 7).
  • Equip from Mog Satchel / Sack / Case allowed (requires a client addon).
  • Explorer Moogle teleports available from level 1 (retail: 10).
  • Records of Eminence timed records active.
  • Synergy crafting enabled.
  • Login Campaign active — daily rewards for logging in.
  • Daily tally / Gobbie Mystery Box — 50 points/day (retail: 10), eligible after 1 day (retail: 45).
  • ENM key-item cooldown — 0h (retail: 120h).
  • No regime level penalty — REGIME_REWARD_THRESHOLD = 150 (retail: 15).
  • EXP rings — multiple ownership allowed, no one-per-week limit, up to 10 Divine Might earrings.
  • Homepoint teleport system enabled.

docs.title: Custom NPCs and content
docs.text: Beyond the settings tweaks above, Legendary adds a stack of custom NPCs and hunt systems. The big ones each have their own page; the rest are summarized inline.

docs.title: Reisenjima Henge hub
docs.text:
Three custom NPCs stand side-by-side at Reisenjima Henge — the endgame zone that anchors the bulk of Legendary's progression loop.

NPC Position What it does Hunt: Hub see Hunting League Shows rank & marks, unlocks ranks, reward shop Hunt: Spawner see Hunting League Pops current-rank NMs on demand Armor Vendor (2.49, 5.51, -12.18) Endgame armor for seals — see Gear Vendors Weapons Vendor (-0.51, 5.51, -12.18) Endgame weapons for seals — see Gear Vendors
  • Hunting League is the rank-based NM hunting system that drives all progression. Five ranks, ~3 NMs per rank, mark currency, reward shop. → Full details
  • Armor Vendor and Weapons Vendor sell tiered gear (Bronze / Silver / Gold) for the three seal currencies. → Full catalogs

docs.title: Reforge System (Gwora Corridor)
docs.text:
Two NPCs at Gwora Corridor drive a parallel NM-farm-to-armor pipeline focused on AF / Relic / Empyrean armor.

NPC Position What it does Reforge Spawner (10.0, 0.0, 0.0) Pops one of three NM pools (Sky Gods / Unity NMs / Abyssea NMs) Reforge Vendor (15.0, 0.0, 0.0) Upgrades base → +1 → +2 → +3 for marks

Three currencies (AF Marks, Relic Marks, Empyrean Marks) track separately. Every kill drops a base piece and marks for its track. All 22 jobs supported. → Full details

docs.text:
GM Home hosts five clusters of custom NPCs spanning starter setup, character upgrades, weekly activities, combat testing, and commerce. Use !gmhome from anywhere in-game to warp there instantly. Positions auto-update from the live Lua source files.

All NPCs are in GM Home (zone 210). Positions shown as (x, y, z).

docs.title: Custom HNM system
docs.text:
Legendary runs a hybrid HNM pop system that blends era-style timed rotation with retail-style QM pops:

  • NQ kings (Fafnir, Behemoth, Aspidochelone, etc.) rotate on a timed window, persisting across server restarts.
  • HQ kings (Nidhogg, King Behemoth, etc.) drop via QM placeholders.
  • Respawn timers persist across restarts — crashes don't reset the clock.
  • Each king's respawn window is tuned individually (e.g. Fafnir's is 21–24h).

docs.title: World-first announcements
docs.text:
The server broadcasts to everyone online when a milestone is first achieved:

  • First player death (server-wide bragging rights)
  • First level-up to each level per job (e.g. "First WAR to hit 75")
  • First NM kills for tracked HNMs
  • Winners are recorded permanently, so the title stays attributed even after restarts.

docs.title: Background systems
docs.text:
System-level modules that change behavior server-wide without adding NPCs. You probably won't notice them directly — but you'll notice their absence on a vanilla server.

Module What it changes Always-Popped NMs Every NM in Abyssea (all 10 zones), Escha (Zi'Tah + Ru'Aun), Reisenjima, and Reisenjima Sanctorium auto-spawns at server start and respawns 30 seconds after death. No trade pop, no key item, no atmacite, no cruor — just walk in and fight. HNMs and wave bosses included. Reisenjima Henge is excluded so the Hunting League's on-demand spawner can keep working. Unlimited Visitant (Abyssea) Every player gets permanent Visitant status the moment they zone into any Abyssea area. No timer, no eject to Searing Ward, no pearl/atma farming just to stay alive. Same mechanism retail uses for GMs, applied to everyone. Homepoint Heal Every homepoint visit restores full HP & MP. No more relying on a healer at the crystal. Persistent NM Time of Death NM respawn timers survive crashes and restarts. Currently tracks Behemoth (21–24h window), with more NMs addable. Disable Zone-In Cutscenes Suppresses every auto-cutscene that fires when you zone into an area with a mission/quest stage that would normally trigger one. Side effects (position resets, charvar updates, key item grants) still happen — only the cutscene playback is skipped. Talk to the NPC manually if you want to see it. Auto Unstick Server-side watchdog that clears stuck event state from any character on zone-in. If your character is wedged in a "still in cutscene" state, just zone (or log out and back in) and the watchdog releases you. Also defuses the Mog House 2F unlock cutscene loop that traps some characters. RoE "Gain Experience" Always On The Records of Eminence 4-hour timed reward for "gain 5000 EXP" is active in every slot, every day — was 3 slots per week by default. (There's also a GM-only !gainexp command for instant claim, but players earn this the normal way by gaining EXP.) Conquest Regional NPCs Always Up Bastok, Windurst, and San d'Oria regional NPCs stay visible regardless of which nation owns conquest. No "come back next week" walls. Mission Wardrobe Unlocks Hitting mission milestones unlocks Mog Wardrobe slots. Currently: Zilart completion → Mog Wardrobe 3 unlocked. Max-Size Mog Wardrobes at Creation All 8 Mog Wardrobes are pre-sized to maximum capacity on character creation. By default, wardrobes 1-8 start at 0 slots until manually expanded; this skips that and gives every new character full storage from minute one. New Player Linkshell New characters automatically receive a designated server linkshell at character creation. Login Announcements Broadcasts a server-wide message when a player logs in, so the community knows when familiar names are online. First-99 Timestamp Tracker The first time any of a character's jobs hits level 99, the timestamp is stamped permanently into a charvar. Powers the "Fastest 1 → 99" leaderboard on the Community page. Lock-once — re-leveling another job to 99 doesn't overwrite the stamp. Chocobo Raising QoL Faster chocobo growth (2 days to chick stage), higher endgame stat caps (riding speed 120, endurance), tuned for active raising. Wish Upon a Star Workaround Patches the Bastok "Wish Upon a Star" weather-gate quest that's otherwise impossible without a specific weather event. SoA Imprimatur Gate Removed Seekers of Adoulin missions no longer require Imprimatur key items or fame. Talk to the NPC, get the mission. Garrison Placeholder Data Supplies temporary NPC appearance data (looks, weapons) for Garrison content so it runs even without captured units. Organized by level cap × nation.

docs.title: What's NOT changed
docs.text:
For reference, these are at retail defaults on this server:

  • Mob HP / accuracy / damage multipliers
  • Mob movement speed
  • Auction House fee structure
  • Enmity cap (30,000)
  • Sneak/Invis/Deodorize durations
  • Old cure formula / old magic damage (both off — uses modern formulas)
  • Fishing is disabled (server-wide)

docs.title: Background Systems
docs.text:
These are server-level systems that run silently in the background — no NPC to talk to, no command to type. Most players encounter them indirectly: you zone into Abyssea and an NM is already up, or you get stuck in a cutscene loop and zoning out fixes it.

This page explains what each system does so you know what's happening when you run into it.

docs.title: Abyssea Always-Popped
docs.text:
Every NM across all ten Abyssea zones, Escha (Zi'Tah + Ru'Aun), Reisenjima, and Reisenjima Sanctorium auto-spawns at server start and respawns 30 seconds after death.

No pop requirements. No trade items. No key items. No atmacite. No cruor threshold. Just walk in and start fighting.

This covers HNMs and wave bosses in those zones as well. If you're looking for a specific Abyssea NM, it's already up — or it'll be back in half a minute.

Reisenjima Henge excluded

The Henge itself is excluded from the always-pop system so the Hunting League's on-demand Spawner keeps working correctly.

docs.title: Unlimited Visitant
docs.text:
In retail Abyssea, Visitant status has a time limit — your clock ticks down, and when it runs out you get ejected. On Legendary, every player receives permanent Visitant status the moment they zone into any Abyssea area.

No timer. No decay. No atma farming just to stay inside. Zone in and stay as long as you want.

docs.title: Auto-Unstick
docs.text:
A server-side watchdog clears stuck event state whenever you zone in. If your character is locked in a cutscene loop or stuck in a "still in event" state, the fix is simple:

  1. Zone out (walk to a zone line, or use any teleport command).
  2. Zone back in.
  3. The watchdog fires on zone-in and releases the stuck state.

Tip

If zoning once doesn't clear it, log out and back in — that's a full zone-in cycle and always triggers the watchdog.

docs.title: Zone-In Cutscenes Disabled
docs.text:
Auto-cutscenes that fire when you zone into a mission-heavy area are suppressed. If you've ever had the game lock you into a five-minute cutscene just because you walked through a zone line, you know why this exists.

Any side effects that the cutscene would have produced — position resets, charvar updates, key item grants — still happen. Only the video playback is skipped.

If you want to watch a specific cutscene, talk to the relevant NPC manually.

docs.title: RoE "Gain Experience" — Always Available
docs.text:
The Records of Eminence "Gain Experience" objective (earn 5,000 EXP in 4 hours) is active in every slot, every day. On retail it's limited to three slots per week.

As a player, you earn this the normal way — just gain EXP and the reward fires on the natural cycle. There is a !gainexp command that triggers the reward instantly, but it's GM-only and not available to regular players.

docs.title: World-First Announcements
docs.text:
When a player achieves a server-first milestone, the server broadcasts it to everyone online. Tracked milestones include:

  • First player death on the server (yes, this one is tracked)
  • First level-up to 99 per job (e.g., "First WAR to hit 99")
  • First kills of tracked HNMs

These are stored permanently — a title stays attributed to the correct player even after server restarts. If you're racing for a world-first, everyone will know when it happens.

docs.title: Chocobo Raising
docs.text:
Chocobo raising is tuned for faster results:

  • 2-day chick cycle (faster than retail)
  • Higher stat caps — riding speed up to 120, higher endurance ceiling
  • Active raising is balanced around the faster growth curve

If you want a high-stat mount, raising is worth the investment.

docs.title: SoA Imprimatur Gate Removed
docs.text:
Seekers of Adoulin missions no longer require Imprimatur currency or fame to progress. Just talk to the NPC and accept the mission.

If you've ever hit the Imprimatur wall on retail (or on a standard private server), this won't be a problem here.

docs.title: Conquest Regional NPCs Always Up
docs.text:
Bastok, Windurst, and San d'Oria regional NPCs are permanently visible, regardless of which nation holds conquest standing in each region.

On retail, regional NPCs disappear when their nation loses the region — leaving you to come back next week. On Legendary, they're always there.

docs.title: Server Economy
docs.text:
A live, anonymous snapshot of Legendary's economy and population — how much gil is in circulation, how busy the Auction House is, and how many hunters are around.

How fresh is this?

These figures are a build-time snapshot, refreshed every time the site is rebuilt — not a live ticker. For the real-time online count, watch the status badge in the site header or ask in Discord. No individual player is named here; this is a macro view, and GM / test characters are excluded so the numbers reflect the real player economy.

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text:
A live snapshot of the server economy and population. All figures exclude GM / test characters and refresh each time the site is rebuilt.

Metric Value Gil in circulation 3.76B gil Players online now 35 Characters (non-GM) 285 Active in last 7 days 284 AH listings (live) 593 Cumulative playtime 96 days, 2 hours

docs.title: Gil Supply
docs.text:
Total gil held by player characters — the money supply. Gil sitting in Auction House escrow (unsold listings) and on GM characters is not counted.

Measure Value Total gil in circulation 3,760,503,041 gil Characters holding gil 203 Average per character 18,524,645 gil Median per character 5,392,102 gil Wealthiest 10% hold 60.4% of all gil

The gap between the average and the median is the inequality signal: when the average sits far above the median, a handful of wealthy hunters are pulling the mean up while most players hold far less.

docs.title: Auction House Depth
docs.text:
Open Auction House listings right now. The market-maker (an NPC seller, AH-Jeuno) keeps a price floor and a deep catalog of gear on the shelf; player listings are everything posted by real characters.

Measure Value Live listings (total) 593 — Market-maker (AH-Jeuno) 525 — Player-listed 68 Distinct items available 348 Total shelf value (asking) 252,647,955 gil

The market-maker exists to keep gear available and to set a price floor so player listings can't be undercut into the ground. It's a one-way shelf: players buy from it, which steadily drains gil out of the economy.

docs.title: Market Velocity
docs.text:
Completed Auction House sales over recent windows. Gil volume is the total that changed hands; gil sunk is the portion spent buying from the market-maker, which removes that gil from the economy for good.

Window Lots sold Gil volume Gil sunk to AH Last 24 hours 124 75,163,061 gil 23,370,000 gil Last 7 days 1,983 696,651,978 gil 504,920,000 gil Last 30 days 1,983 696,651,978 gil 504,920,000 gil

A healthy economy needs gil sinks — ways for gil to leave circulation so prices stay meaningful. Every purchase from the market-maker is a sink, which is why we track it separately from player-to-player volume.

docs.text: Common questions about playing on Legendary FFXI. If you have a question that isn't answered here, ask in our Discord or open an issue on the project repo.

docs.title: How do I connect to the server?
docs.text: See Getting Started → Install the Client and Connect to Server for the full walkthrough.

docs.title: Do I need a Square Enix account or game license?
docs.text: No. Legendary runs against a private server built on LandSandBoat. You only need the FFXI client itself, not an active SE subscription.

docs.title: How do I create a character?
docs.text: Once connected, the standard FFXI character-creation flow runs as usual. Every new character starts at the configured starting level, full inventory, all maps + outpost warps, and the starting gil bundle listed on the home page.

docs.title: Why does my character feel weak compared to retail at the same level?
docs.text: Stats are tuned for this server's faster progression curve, but combat is balanced around the level-99 cap with rebalanced gear. If you feel weak, check the Gear Vendors page — the Hunt Mark currencies are the fastest path to iLvl 119 gear.

docs.title: How do I earn Hunt Marks?
docs.text: Kill the NMs at the Hunting League Spawner. Each NM gives points scaled by tier; higher tiers give more. Unlock tiers using the Hub NPC at the hunt zone.

docs.title: What's the difference between the Hunting League NPC and the Reforge System NPC?
docs.text:
• Hunting League — entry-to-mid-tier gear sold for Hunt Marks (Bronze/Silver/Gold seals).
  • Reforge System — AF/Relic/Empyrean reforge upgrades. Drops base pieces + currency by killing categorized NMs (Sky Gods → AF Marks, Unity NMs → Relic Marks, Abyssea NMs → Empyrean Marks).

docs.title: How does the Augment Moogle differ from the Augment Sage?
docs.text:
• Augment Moogle stamps a single augment from a catalyst item onto a piece of gear. One catalyst, one augment.
  • Augment Sage is a rank system that multiplies augment values (up to 5× at top rank) plus per-NM affinity bonuses. Talk to the Sage to track and rank up.

docs.title: Where's the full list of player commands?
docs.text: Reference → Player Commands — every player command, with parameter types and descriptions. Each is tagged upstream or custom so you can tell which are server-specific.

docs.title: What does !mystats show me?
docs.text: A complete dump of every stat your character has, including bonuses from gear and active buffs. Useful for verifying that a piece of gear is actually doing what its tooltip says. See the !mystats entry for the full output format.

docs.title: What does !gainexp do?
docs.text: Instantly claims the "Gain Experience" RoE timed record reward: +1500 EXP, +300 sparks, +300 accolades, and one Copper Aman Voucher. Available on demand — no cooldown. See !gainexp.

docs.title: Can I auto-spend job points / merits?
docs.text: Yes — !autojp and !automerits. Both spread points breadth-first across categories on your current main job, so no single category gets maxed before others get a look-in. See !autojp and !automerits.

docs.title: How do I find other players?
docs.text:
• Leaderboards — top players by Hunt Marks, NM kills, lifetime currency earned.
  • Player Profiles — browse individual character pages.
  • Discord — live chat, group-up posts, server announcements.

docs.title: What are Player Trusts?
docs.text: A custom system where you can summon other registered players as Trust-style NPCs. See Player Trusts for unlock requirements and the registered-pair list.

docs.title: Can I play solo?
docs.text: Yes. Almost all custom content (Hunting League, Reforge System, Dungeons, Weekly Hunts) can be soloed at the cap. Difficulty is gear-checked, not group-size-checked.

docs.title: The server's down / I can't connect. What do I do?
docs.text:
1. Check the Discord #server-status channel first — outages and maintenance windows are announced there.
  2. If the server is up but you can't connect, verify your client is pointed at the right login server (see Connect to Server).

docs.title: I think I found a bug. Where do I report it?
docs.text: Two options: - GitHub Issues — preferred for reproducible bugs with clear steps. - Discord #bug-reports — for quick reports or "is this intended?" questions.

docs.title: My character got stuck / I lost an item / something broke. Can a GM help?
docs.text: Ping a GM in Discord. Specify your character name, what happened, and roughly when. Most stuck-character and accidental-deletion situations can be resolved.

docs.title: What's different about this server vs. retail / vs. plain LandSandBoat?
docs.text:
The What's Custom page is the authoritative list. Highlights:

  • Faster EXP / CP / drop rates (current multipliers shown on the home page)
  • Full subjob from character creation
  • 99 starting level cap, all maps + outpost warps granted at creation
  • Custom Hunting League, Reforge System, Augment Sage, Player Trusts, Weekly Hunt Board, and Dungeons systems
  • Every player command listed in Reference → Player Commands

docs.title: Are character files / progress safe? Are there backups?
docs.text:
Yes — daily backups of the character database are taken. In a worst case, the most you'd lose is a few hours.

Have a question that should be on this page? Ping a GM in Discord and we'll add it.

docs.title: Player Trusts
docs.text:
Party with someone for long enough and you both unlock each other as a personal Trust — a permanent in-game bond that you can summon for a stat boost, and upgrade over time.

Summary

Party up with another character. Stay in the same zone. Once your shared party time reaches 30 minutes, you both automatically unlock each other as Trusts. Talk to the Companion Master at GM Home to summon any unlocked friend, or spend gil to upgrade their tier.

docs.title: How unlocking works
docs.text:
The friendship counter increments once per minute, but only while ALL of these are true:

  • Both characters are online
  • Both are in the same party (any role, leader doesn't matter)
  • Both are in the same zone

The counter does not decrement when conditions stop being met — it just pauses. You can leave each other's party, log out, take a week off, then resume; your accumulated minutes wait for you.

At 30 minutes of shared party-in-zone time

, both characters get an unlock notification:

[Companion Master] You have unlocked Jbae as a Trust, kupo! Visit the Companion Master at GM Home.

The unlock is permanent. Logout/zone changes don't undo it.

docs.title: The Companion Master NPC
docs.text:
At GM Home, position (x = -3.000, y = 0.000, z = -30.000, rot = 128).

Talk to them to see a menu:

Companion Master
  Jbae [Bronze]
  Bdr [Silver]
  Wanheda [Gold]
  Close

Each entry shows the friend's name and their current Trust tier. Pick one to enter a sub-menu:

Jbae [Bronze]
  Set as Active Trust
  Quick Buff (30min stat boost)
  Upgrade to Silver (500,000 gil)
  << Back

docs.title: How to upgrade
docs.text:
Upgrades happen at the Companion Master, paid in gil, and bump a friend's tier one step at a time (Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum → Mythic). Each step:

  1. Pick the friend from the Companion Master's roster — their tier is shown next to the name.
  2. Choose Upgrade to <next tier> from the sub-menu.
  3. The transaction is atomic: if you have enough gil, the tier bumps and the gil leaves your wallet in the same instant. If you don't, you get a "You need N gil" message and nothing is charged.
  4. Each upgrade is independent per friend — maxing Jbae costs you nothing toward Bdr.

The gil ladder per friend:

Step Cost Cumulative Bronze (auto on unlock) — 0 → Silver 500,000 500,000 → Gold 1,500,000 2,000,000 → Platinum 4,000,000 6,000,000 → Mythic 10,000,000 16,000,000

So a Mythic Trust represents 16M gil sunk into one friendship. With Legendary's 100× quest gil and 10× mob gil rates, that's achievable but meaningful — not a casual purchase.

docs.title: Where the upgrade actually goes
docs.text:
This is the part that confuses people. The Trust system has two summon modes, and each tier bump improves both at once, but on different entities:

Catalog field Buffs… When it applies statBonus, hpBonus, mpBonus, buffDurationMin You (the casting player) Only when you pick Quick Buff at the NPC — a status-effect-style flat bonus on your character trustMult (multiplies trustBaseMods) The summoned Trust mob Only when you cast the slot's spell to summon the real follower

Concretely: upgrade Jbae to Mythic → - Casting Quick Buff on yourself: you get +20 to all stats, +250 HP, +125 MP, 2 hour duration. - Summoning Jbae as a real Trust: the spawned mob gets every base mod (HPP / DEF / MEVA / ATT / ACC / MATT / MACC / Haste / STR / DEX / VIT auras) multiplied by 2.0× — so the follower hits harder, lives longer, and projects a bigger stat aura onto you.

The Quick Buff and the real Trust are mutually exclusive moments — you cast one or the other — but a higher-tier friend strengthens whichever path you choose at cast time.

docs.title: As a real Trust (recommended)
docs.text:
You have five Trust slots. Each slot maps to a specific hijacked Trust spell in your spell book. Assign a friend to a slot via the Companion Master, then cast that slot's spell to summon them.

Slot Cast this spell to summon your assigned friend 1 Trust: Kuyin Hathdenna 2 Trust: Rosulatia 3 Trust: Teodor 4 Trust: King Of Hearts 5 Trust: Morimar

The mob that spawns:

  • Wears your friend's race (captured the moment you first unlocked each other)
  • Displays your friend's character name above its head
  • Has combat AI just like any Trust — follows you, attacks what you fight, despawns on zone change
  • Has tier-scaled stats — see the table below

You can have all five slots filled at once. Cast multiple spells and you get a full alliance of friend-Trusts. Each slot tracks its own friend assignment; switching a friend between slots is free at the Companion Master.

Why those weird spell names? Engine-side, we hijack five obscure Walk of Echoes / Records of Eminence Trusts (none of which players normally obtain) to run our own logic — those spells are the "slots" all your friend-Trusts use. The mob you actually summon is fully customized; only the spell's listed name in your book is fixed. Pro tip: rename your macros to "Summon Bdr" / "Summon Jbae" / etc. instead of using the default spell names.

docs.title: Quick buff
docs.text:
Pick Quick Buff on a friend for a low-effort, no-cast stat boost (the old v1 behavior, kept around). Immediate, lasts 30-120 minutes depending on tier, applies flat bonuses:

  • +stat to all 7 main stats (STR/DEX/VIT/AGI/INT/MND/CHR)
  • +HP flat health
  • +MP flat magic

Only one Quick Buff can be active at a time — re-summoning replaces it. No visible buff icon; the chat message tells you the duration and bonuses.

docs.title: Upgrade tiers
docs.text: Five tiers per friend. Upgrade costs are paid in gil at the Companion Master and are independent per friend — maxing Jbae costs you nothing toward Bdr.

docs.title: Cost and duration ladder
docs.text: Tier Duration (Quick Buff) Gil from previous tier Cumulative Bronze 30 min (free on unlock) 0 Silver 45 min 500,000 500,000 Gold 60 min 1,500,000 2,000,000 Plat. 90 min 4,000,000 6,000,000 Mythic 120 min 10,000,000 16,000,000

docs.title: Full Quick Buff ledger
docs.text:
Picking Quick Buff at the Companion Master applies these 9 mods to you (the casting player) for the duration above. The statBonus field is a single value that lifts all 7 main stats simultaneously — at Mythic that's +20 to every one of STR / DEX / VIT / AGI / INT / MND / CHR.

Mod on caster Bronze Silver Gold Plat. Mythic STR +3 +6 +10 +14 +20 DEX +3 +6 +10 +14 +20 VIT +3 +6 +10 +14 +20 AGI +3 +6 +10 +14 +20 INT +3 +6 +10 +14 +20 MND +3 +6 +10 +14 +20 CHR +3 +6 +10 +14 +20 HP (flat) +20 +50 +100 +150 +250 MP (flat) +10 +25 +50 +75 +125

Only one Quick Buff can be active at a time across all your friends — casting a different friend's Quick Buff replaces the active one.

docs.title: Leaderboard credit
docs.text: Each unlock bumps your Trusts_Unlocked counter, which feeds a future "Most Friends" leaderboard slot. Mythic-tier upgrades don't add extra credit there — every friend counts once, regardless of tier — but they do reflect on your wallet.

docs.title: Tier scaling for the Trust mob
docs.text:
When you summon the real Trust (not the Quick Buff), the spawned follower mob gets every mod in catalog.trustBaseMods multiplied by the friend's tier. Eleven mods total, four functional groups:

Mod on the Trust mob Bronze (1×) Silver (1.25×) Gold (1.5×) Plat. (1.75×) Mythic (2×) HPP (% extra HP on the mob) +20% +25% +30% +35% +40% DEF +50 +62.5 +75 +87.5 +100 MEVA (magic evasion) +30 +37.5 +45 +52.5 +60 ATT +50 +62.5 +75 +87.5 +100 ACC +30 +37.5 +45 +52.5 +60 MATT (magic attack) +30 +37.5 +45 +52.5 +60 MACC (magic accuracy) +30 +37.5 +45 +52.5 +60 HASTE_GEAR (1/1024ths) 150 (~14.6%) 188 (~18.3%) 225 (~22.0%) 262 (~25.6%) 300 (~29.3%) STR (aura — buffs you too) +15 +18.75 +22.5 +26.25 +30 DEX (aura) +15 +18.75 +22.5 +26.25 +30 VIT (aura) +15 +18.75 +22.5 +26.25 +30

The three stat mods at the bottom act as auras: they buff both the Trust and any party member in range — so they stack on top of any STR/DEX/VIT you already have from gear and buffs.

docs.title: Power budget at a glance
docs.text:
If you'd rather skim than read the cells:

Tier Quick Buff sum (7 stats / HP / MP) Real Trust combined power Bronze +21 / +20 / +10 baseline Silver +42 / +50 / +25 ~1.6× Bronze Gold +70 / +100 / +50 ~2.2× Bronze Plat. +98 / +150 / +75 ~3.1× Bronze Mythic +140 / +250 / +125 ~4.0× Bronze

The real-Trust path scales faster than its trustMult suggests because the multiplier compounds across HPP (more HP to start with), ATT (more damage per hit), Haste (more hits per second), and the aura stat stick — each one boosts the next.

docs.title: What's NOT scaled by the tier upgrade
docs.text:
Worth knowing what you're not buying:

  • Job, AI, and spell repertoire. The mob's job is locked to whichever underlying Trust got hijacked for that slot (slot 1 = GEO, slot 5 = BST, etc.). A Mythic Trust doesn't gain new spells — it casts the same spells harder.
  • AGI / INT / MND / CHR auras. Only STR/DEX/VIT are in trustBaseMods. The mob's own stats still benefit from the per-tier multiplier on its base values, but those four don't project onto you as auras. If you want a mage-oriented Trust to push INT/MND onto the party, add lines to trustBaseMods in the catalog.
  • Friendship unlock state. The original 30-min unlock work is a one-time event; tiers are a separate PT_Tier_<id> CharVar that starts at 1 (Bronze) on unlock.
  • Spell name in your book. Engine-side limitation — the cast bar still says "Trust: Kuyin Hathdenna" even after Jbae is in that slot. Rename your macros to your friends' names; the floating nameplate above the spawned mob shows the friend correctly.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Spell names in your book are fixed. Engine doesn't expose per-cast spell renaming — the client looks display names up from its own DAT files. Workaround: rename your macros to your friends' names, and rely on the floating name above the mob (which IS the friend's name) for visual identification. With 5 slots assigned to 5 friends, the cast bar text becomes muscle memory anyway.
  • Face capture is recorded but not yet applied. We store the friend's face number at unlock time (PT_Face_<id> CharVar) but setModelId uses race-based whole-body models. A future tweak could construct a full look hex via setLook to use the exact face — left for a future iteration.
  • Cross-zone unlock progress. The 30-min counter requires both characters in the same zone every minute. Spreading the time across multiple zones doesn't accumulate.

docs.title: Tuning knobs
docs.text:
All in modules/custom/lua/player_trusts_catalog.lua:

  • unlockMinutes — change the friendship threshold (default 30)
  • tickIntervalSec — how often we re-check parties (default 60s)
  • tiers — full table of tier bonuses, durations, and gil costs
  • npcPos — where the Companion Master stands

Reload the module after editing — no server restart required.

docs.title: This Week's Featured Hunt
docs.text:
Each week a single NM per Hunting League tier is designated as the Featured Hunt. The first kill of that NM during the ISO week awards 2× Hunt Marks on top of the normal reward — a meaningful bonus for players who coordinate around it.

The Featured Hunt rotates automatically at the start of each ISO week (Monday 00:00 UTC). To see which NMs are currently featured, use the in-game command:

!featured

First-Kill Bonus

The 2× marks apply to the first kill only per week. After that, the NM still drops normal marks — it never goes dry. Clear it early for the bonus, then keep farming.

docs.title: Active Events
docs.text:
Seasonal bonus-mark events multiply the Hunt Marks you earn from kills for a limited window. Only one applies at a time — if two overlap, the higher-priority one wins. For the live bonus, use !events in-game.

No bonus-mark events are active or scheduled right now. Watch #announcements on Discord for the next one.

Event Announcements

Seasonal events — including double-marks weekends and holiday content — are announced in the #announcements channel on Discord before going live. Keep an eye there for upcoming events.

docs.title: Gil Exchange — turning gil into Hunt Marks
docs.text:
Sitting on more gil than you'll ever spend? The Gil Exchange in GM Home converts raw gil into Hunt Marks, the currency that drives the Hunting League. The rates are deliberately steep — this is a last-resort sink for rich players, not a shortcut around hunting.

Summary

A gil sink in GM Home that buys Hunt Marks with your spare gil at intentionally poor rates — for players drowning in gil who still want progression.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: The Gil Exchange is in the gil-services row at GM Home. Speak to it to open the menu — your current gil shows at the top, and your Hunt Mark total is confirmed after each trade.

docs.title: Exchange bundles
docs.text:
Each bundle is a single click that spends gil for Hunt Marks. Bigger bundles give a slightly better ratio:

You pay You receive Rate 100k gil 1 Hunt Mark 100,000 gil each 1M gil 12 Hunt Marks 83,333 gil each 10M gil 150 Hunt Marks 66,667 gil each

Hunting NMs is still by far the fastest way to earn marks — think of this as a way to put a runaway gil pile to work, not a replacement for the hunt.

docs.title: Home Point Network — GM Home
docs.text:
A Home Point crystal stands in GM Home that works like a full home-point terminal: set your home point here, then free-warp to home points all across Vana'diel — no attunement, no gil, no gates.

Summary

A Home Point crystal in GM Home. Set your home point there and warp, for free, to home points across the whole world — every major city, the Adoulin and Aht Urhgan regions, the past, Sky, Sea, and dozens of dungeons and fields.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: The Home Point crystal sits in GM Home, in the travel-NPC cluster on the east side — alongside the other warp services. Using it is always free: no gil cost and no attunement, so every destination is open from your first visit.

docs.title: Setting your home point
docs.text: Choose Set home point here and GM Home becomes your home point — you'll return here whenever you're knocked out and raised, or any time you use a home-point warp. It also registers GM Home as a destination on the wider home-point network, so other crystals out in the world can send you back.

docs.title: Where you can warp
docs.text:
Talk to the crystal, choose Warp to a home point, pick a region, then pick a destination. Long regions are split across pages — use the Next and Prev buttons to scroll.

The crystal reaches 121 home points spread across 12 regions — effectively the entire home-point network in one place:

Region Home points San d'Oria 11 Bastok 12 Windurst 15 Jeuno 10 Aht Urhgan 5 Adoulin 4 Ulbuka 7 Other Towns 10 Past [S] 6 Sky 6 Sea 5 Dungeons & Fields 30 Total 121

Last updated: 2026-06-14 13:15 UTC

docs.title: Race Changer
docs.text:
Want a fresh look? The Race Changer in GM Home lets you change your character's race and pick a new face for a flat gil fee. It's purely cosmetic and applies instantly — your level, jobs, and progress are untouched.

Summary

Pay a one-time gil fee at the Race Changer in GM Home to switch your race and face — instant, cosmetic, and nothing else about your character changes.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: The Race Changer stands at the end of the gil-services row in GM Home. Talk to it, choose a new race and face, then confirm.

docs.title: What it costs and what you get
docs.text:
A race change costs 100M gil (100,000,000 gil), charged once when you confirm. You can switch to any of the 8 races (your current one is left off the list) and pick from 16 faces per race. The change is instant and purely cosmetic — your size, level, jobs, and everything else stay exactly as they were.

Once you confirm, the fee is charged and you rezone for a moment so your new model loads. Any gear your new race can't wear is simply unequipped — pop it back on afterward.

Last updated: 2026-06-14 13:15 UTC

docs.title: Reforge Mark Exchange
docs.text:
The Reforge Exchange lets you convert spare Reforge marks from one line into another, so a surplus you've banked in one track can fund the set you're actually upgrading.

Summary

Trade excess AF, Relic, or Empyrean marks for the line you need at the Reforge Exchange near the Gear Vendors — a small conversion tax keeps each track honest.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text: The Reforge Exchange stands at Gwora-Corridor, right beside the Gear Vendors — the same spot where you turn marks into upgrades.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: The Reforge System runs three parallel upgrade tracks — AF, Relic, and Empyrean — and each track earns and spends its own marks. Hunt long enough and you'll bank far more marks in one track than you can use while another sits short. This NPC lets you rebalance that surplus toward the set you're chasing.

docs.title: Conversions
docs.text:
Each conversion charges a small tax, so trading down a surplus costs you a little but never trivializes a track:

You spend You receive Rate 2 AF Marks 1 Relic Marks 2:1 2 Relic Marks 1 Empy Marks 2:1 3 AF Marks 1 Empy Marks 3:1

docs.title: How to trade
docs.text:
Talk to the NPC and the menu lists each conversion with how many marks you currently hold. Pick a conversion, choose a batch size, and confirm — your source marks are spent and the new marks are added on the spot.

Each visit you can convert in batches of 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 target marks at once (you'll only be offered batches you can afford), so a large surplus can be moved over in a few clicks.

docs.title: Sparks Exchange — Eminence Broker
docs.text:
Records of Eminence shower you with Sparks of Eminence, and once you're capped they pile up with nothing to spend them on. The Eminence Broker (a.k.a. "Sparks Cash") in GM Home buys those sparks back for gil — a steady gil faucet for capped players and a way to drain a maxed-out spark balance.

Summary

Trade your Sparks of Eminence for gil at the Eminence Broker in GM Home — pick a preset amount or cash out everything at once.

docs.title: Where to find the Broker
docs.text: The Eminence Broker stands in the economy corner of GM Home, in the row of gil-service NPCs. Talk to him to convert Sparks of Eminence, Unity Accolades, or Job Points into gil.

docs.title: The exchange rate
docs.text: Sparks: 10 gil each · Accolades: 100 gil each · Job Points: 4,000 gil each

docs.title: Convert amounts
docs.text: Talk to the Broker and the menu shows your current spark balance. Pick one of the preset amounts, or cash out your whole balance in a single click:

docs.title: Sparks of Eminence
docs.text:
10 gil per Spark.

Sparks You receive 1,000 10,000 gil 10,000 100,000 gil 50,000 500,000 gil All your sparks balance × 10 gil

docs.title: Unity Accolades

100 gil per Accolade.

Accolades You receive 500 50,000 gil 5,000 500,000 gil 25,000 2,500,000 gil All your accolades balance × 100 gil

4,000 gil per Job Point.

Job Points You receive 1 4,000 gil 5 20,000 gil 20 80,000 gil All your JP balance × 4,000 gil

The Broker won't let an exchange overflow your gil — if you're near the gil cap, spend some first and come back.

docs.title: Abyssea NMs — Hunt Marks System
docs.text:
Abyssea is home to some of the most powerful Notorious Monsters on the server. Rather than hunting down rare key items to spawn them, Legendary replaces the retail pop system with a Hunt Marks spend: find the ???, pay your marks, and the NM rises right in front of you.

Summary

Spend Hunt Marks at any Abyssea ??? to pop its NM on demand. Kill it with your party for a large Infamy and Gil payout — no key items required.

docs.title: Zones & Difficulty Tiers
docs.text:
Abyssea is divided into three difficulty tiers based on the expansion each zone belongs to. Higher tiers demand more coordination, hit harder, and reward more.

Tier Zones Mark Cost Level HP Visions Konschtat, Tahrongi, La Theine 200 marks 135 4,000,000 Scars Attohwa, Misareaux, Vunkerl 350 marks 145 7,000,000 Heroes Altepa, Uleguerand, Grauberg 500 marks 155 10,000,000

These are not solo targets

All tiers are tuned for a full party of real players. Each NM has dramatically boosted ATK, DEF, accuracy, and evasion on top of its level-scaled stats. Coming in underprepared or alone is likely to end badly.

docs.title: Getting There
docs.text:
Use the !abyssea command to open a zone warp menu:

!abyssea

A two-tier menu appears — pick the expansion tier, then the specific zone. You'll land at a safe camp near the zone entrance.

docs.title: Popping an NM
docs.text:
Each Abyssea NM has a ??? landmark somewhere in the zone. Walk up to it and check:

If you're missing the retail key items (which you almost certainly are — they've been removed from the game):

  1. A menu appears showing the NM name and the Hunt Mark cost.
  2. If you have enough marks, a Pop button is available — confirm it.
  3. Your marks are spent, the NM spawns directly next to you, and it's already claimed to your party.

If you somehow still have the original retail key items, the vanilla pop still works — the ??? will handle it as normal.

Key items from retail

If you had any Abyssea pop key items from retail (Tattered Hippogryph Wing, Cracked Wivre Horn, etc.), they were automatically removed from your inventory when you last logged in. They have no function on this server.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text: Killing a marks-popped NM pays out Infamy and Gil to every member of your party. The payout scales with your party composition.

docs.title: Base rewards by tier
docs.text: Tier Infamy Gil Visions 25 250,000 Scars 40 500,000 Heroes 60 750,000

docs.title: Multipliers
docs.text:
Two bonuses can stack on top of the base reward:

Condition Multiplier 2 or more real players in party ×2.0 No trusts in party ×1.5

These multiply together, so a full party of real players with no trusts earns ×3.0.

docs.title: Full reward table
docs.text:
VisionsScarsHeroes Scenario Mult Infamy Gil Solo, with trusts ×1.0 25 250,000 Solo, no trusts ×1.5 37 375,000 Party, with trusts ×2.0 50 500,000 Party, no trusts ×3.0 75 750,000 Scenario Mult Infamy Gil Solo, with trusts ×1.0 40 500,000 Solo, no trusts ×1.5 60 750,000 Party, with trusts ×2.0 80 1,000,000 Party, no trusts ×3.0 120 1,500,000 Scenario Mult Infamy Gil Solo, with trusts ×1.0 60 750,000 Solo, no trusts ×1.5 90 1,125,000 Party, with trusts ×2.0 120 1,500,000 Party, no trusts ×3.0 180 2,250,000

After the kill a system message confirms your payout and any active multiplier bonus.

docs.title: What to Spend Infamy On
docs.text:
Infamy is spent at the Infamy Vendor in GM Home. The full catalog includes accessories, armor, Relic/Mythic/Aeonic weapons, and more. A few reference points:

Item tier Cost Accessories (Fotia Belt, earrings, rings) 250–300 Infamy Armor pieces (Nyame, Jhakri) 400–800 Infamy Relic / Aeonic weapons 800 Infamy Mythic weapons 10,000 Infamy

A party running Heroes NMs without trusts earns 180 Infamy per kill — enough for a full Nyame body in under 5 kills, and a Mythic weapon in roughly 55 kills.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Bring a healer. Every NM tier is designed to require active healing. The stat boosts are large enough that an undefended party member can be killed in a few hits.
  • Drop your trusts before the kill. The ×1.5 no-trust multiplier is free Infamy. Dismiss them once the NM is engaged and you're confident in your party.
  • The NM respawns after a server restart. If you pop and kill an NM, the ??? is available immediately for the next pop — there's no lockout timer.
  • You need to be the one to land the kill. Only parties where someone gets the killing blow trigger the reward. Don't let a rogue trust finish it off right as you dismiss them.

docs.title: Casino — Lady Luck
docs.text:
Feeling lucky? Lady Luck runs a four-game casino in GM Home where you can gamble your gil on slots, high-low, roulette, and dice. Every game keeps a small house edge, so over time it's a gil sink — but a hot streak can pay out huge, and any single win big enough is shouted to the whole server.

Summary

A four-game gil-sink casino — slots, high-low, roulette, and dice — run by Lady Luck in GM Home. Pick a stake and play; the biggest wins shout server-wide.

docs.title: Where to play
docs.text: Lady Luck holds court in GM Home — step up to the table, pick a game, and place your stake.

docs.title: Placing a bet
docs.text:
Bets are fixed tiers (the menu can't take a typed-in amount) — pick your stake, then your game:

Stakes: 5,000 / 25,000 / 100,000 / 500,000 gil.

Any single win of 2,000,000 gil or more is shouted server-wide — bragging rights included.

docs.title: The games
docs.text:
Game How it works Payouts House edge Slots Spin three reels, match three symbols 7×3 = 150×, Bell×3 = 30×, Melon×3 = 10×, Cherry×3 = 4× ~8.4% High-Low A card 1–13 is shown; bet whether the next is higher or lower Odds-based — safe calls pay barely over 1×, long shots pay big ~8.0% Roulette Single-zero wheel (0–36); bet a colour/odd/even or a single number Even-money 2×, single number 35× ~2.7% even / ~5.4% single Dice Roll 2d6; bet the High (8–12) / Low (2–6) band or Lucky 7 High/Low 2.25×, Lucky 7 5× ~6.2% band / ~16.7% on 7

All payouts are total-return multipliers: a 2× win on a 25,000 gil bet returns 50,000 (a net gain of 25,000), a push returns your bet, and a loss keeps it. The house edge is the long-run cost of playing — small on the even-money bets, bigger on the long-shots that pay the most.

docs.title: Chocobo Derby
docs.text:
Down in GM Home, the Race Caller runs the races. Put gil on a runner and watch it play out — and if you've raised a chocobo of your own that's tough enough, line it up at the gate and bet on yourself.

Summary

Bet gil on chocobo races at the Race Caller in GM Home; raise a strong enough chocobo of your own and you can enter it as a runner for a bigger payout.

docs.title: Where to play
docs.text: The Race Caller stands in the activities row of GM Home. Step up to check the odds board, place a bet, and watch the race play out.

docs.title: Placing a bet
docs.text:
Stakes: 10,000 / 50,000 / 250,000 gil.

Each runner carries odds set by its hidden strength: the long-shots pay the most, the favourites the least. The house keeps about 15% of the fair payout as its cut, and even a heavy favourite always returns at least 1.15× your stake when it wins. Back the wrong bird and you lose your bet.

docs.title: The field
docs.text:
Every race fields 6 runners. If you aren't racing a chocobo of your own, they're all from the house stable; if you are, your bird takes one of the gates. The stable regulars are drawn from this roster:

  • Chocofury · Bolt v. Kweh · Lady Bolt
  • Sir Scratch · Meteor Mike · Yellowcomet
  • Dust Dan · Sandy Sally · Gallop Gus
  • Wark Wonder · Featherluck · Kwehsar

A race runs about 20 seconds of live commentary before the winner crosses the line.

docs.title: Racing your own chocobo
docs.text:
Raised a chocobo of your own? Once it reaches the adolescent stage (or older) you can enter it as a runner instead of just betting on the stable.

Your bird races on its real ability — its strength, endurance, and how much affection you've raised it with all feed its hidden racing form, so a well-loved, well-trained chocobo genuinely out-classes the house runners and races at shorter odds.

And there's a reason to root for your own: winning a race on your chocobo pays an extra 25% on top of the normal payout.

Like the casino, the derby is a long-run gil sink — the house keeps its cut over time — but a well-judged bet, or a champion bird of your own, can still pay off big on the day.

docs.title: Colosseum — Ranked Arena
docs.text:
Think you're the strongest champion on the server? Enroll at the Arena Herald in GM Home and prove it. The Colosseum is an asynchronous, ranked PvP-style arena: you duel level-scaled replicas of other champions to climb an Elo rating ladder — no need to catch your rivals online.

Summary

A ranked arena in GM Home where you duel AI replicas of other champions to climb an Elo ladder, earning Hunt Marks for every win.

docs.title: Where to fight
docs.text:
The Arena Herald stands in GM Home — talk to them to enroll your champion on the ladder, browse the roster of rivals, and accept a duel.

Enrolling snapshots your champion's name, race, job, and level onto the ladder. From then on, anyone can challenge a replica of your champion — and you can challenge theirs — at any time.

docs.title: How a duel works
docs.text:
When you challenge a champion, you fight a level-scaled replica of them — an AI stand-in, so the rival doesn't need to be online.

  • A 3-second countdown gives you a moment to ready up before the replica appears.
  • You have 5 minutes to win. Run out the clock and the duel is forfeit.
  • You can challenge each champion once per day (resets at 00:00 UTC) — pick your matches and come back tomorrow for a rematch.

Duels are fought in GM Home, with the replica spawning right next to you. There's no party play here — it's a one-on-one test of your champion.

docs.title: The rating ladder
docs.text:
Every champion starts at a rating of 1,200 and can never fall below 800. Win a duel and your rating climbs while your opponent's slips; the ladder is zero-sum, so the only way up is through other champions.

A replica scales to the rival's rating, not their gear — a higher-rated champion is proof of a dangerous fighter. The tougher the rating, the higher the replica's level (from 99 up to a cap of 205) and the deeper its HP pool (2× to 10× a normal mob's health). Climbing the ladder literally makes your own champion harder for others to beat.

Because the ladder is zero-sum, ratings stay honest and self-balancing: there's always a beatable opponent near the bottom and a fearsome one at the top. Your current and best ratings, wins, and losses are all tracked for the leaderboards.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
Duels pay out in Hunt Marks, the server's main currency:

  • Win: 150 marks — plus a bonus for punching up and beating a higher-rated champion.
  • Loss: 25 marks as a consolation, so a defeat is never a total loss.

The bigger the gap when you beat someone rated above you, the sweeter the haul — the ladder rewards bravery as much as skill.

docs.title: Scheduled Invasions — Defend Al Zahbi
docs.text:
Eight times a day the Voidsent pour into Al Zahbi, and it falls to whoever's around to throw them back. Invasions are a Besieged-style outpost defense: escalating waves of enemies that grow with the size of your defending force, capped off by a boss. Survive the assault and every defender shares in the spoils.

Summary

An eight-times-daily Besieged-style defense of Al Zahbi — waves of Voidsent that scale with how many defenders show up, ending in a boss, rewarding marks and Infamy to all who hold the line.

docs.title: When it happens
docs.text:
The Voidsent strike 8 times a day, at 00:00 UTC and 03:00 UTC and 06:00 UTC and 09:00 UTC and 12:00 UTC and 15:00 UTC and 18:00 UTC and 21:00 UTC.

  • A server-wide warning shouts 5 minutes before each window so you can rally at Al Zahbi.
  • The assault only fires if at least one defender is standing in Al Zahbi when the window opens — it stays armed for up to 10 minutes waiting for someone to show. No defenders, no invasion.

Just be in Al Zahbi when a window opens and you're automatically a defender — there's nothing to sign up for.

docs.title: The waves
docs.text:
The assault rolls in as a ladder of escalating waves, each tougher than the last, before the Voidsent commander itself appears:

Wave Enemy level Vanguard 110 Shock Troops 125 Dreadguard 140 Apex Guard 155 The Warlord 165 Voidsent Warlord (boss) 175

The final wave brings its own trash alongside the boss — clear them all and the boss to win.

docs.title: Scaling and time limit
docs.text: The more defenders who answer the call, the larger each wave — bring friends and the horde swells to match. The whole assault, from the first wave to the boss, must be cleared within 15 minutes. Hold the line and fell the boss before the clock runs out to claim victory.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
Every defender present is paid out — credit goes to anyone in Al Zahbi at the relevant moment:

  • 150 Hunt Marks for each wave cleared.
  • 1,125 Hunt Marks + 100 Infamy on a full victory (the boss falls). This is one of the few sources of Infamy outside the dungeons.
  • 150 Hunt Marks as a consolation if the clock beats the defense.

Victory also drops gear-vendor medals — a guaranteed Kindreds Medal haul, plus a guaranteed Demons Medal drop.

Those medals feed the Armor and Weapons gear vendors (see the !hunt gear loop), so a strong turnout at invasions is a steady route to better equipment.

docs.title: Provisioners' League
docs.text:
A non-combat league for anglers and crafters. The League Steward at Reisenjima Henge tracks your fishing weigh-ins and high-quality craft turn-ins, awarding League Points that climb a five-rank ladder — and every rank-up permanently boosts the marks you earn around the server.

Summary

Fish and turn in HQ crafts at the League Steward in Reisenjima Henge to earn League Points; climbing the five-rank ladder grants a permanent, stacking mark bonus.

docs.title: Where to join
docs.text: Seek out the League Steward at Reisenjima Henge — he keeps the books for both anglers and crafters. Talk to him to check your rank, your League Point total, and this week's featured fish.

docs.title: Earning League Points
docs.text:
There are two ways to earn League Points:

Fishing weigh-ins — every fish you catch is worth points that scale with the fish's skill: the tougher the catch, the more it pays. On top of that:

  • A big fish (the ruler-measured monsters) is worth 2× points.
  • A legendary catch is league gold — worth 10× points.
  • This week's featured fish pays a 3× bonus — a rotating target that keeps the weekly race fresh and is always something a normal angler can land.

Crafting turn-ins — every high-quality (HQ) item you hand in at the server's Crafting Exchange also credits League Points alongside its usual reward, so your crafting progress counts here too.

There's also a weekly leaderboard scored on the points you earn that week — a fresh race every week, separate from your lifetime total.

docs.title: The rank ladder
docs.text:
Your lifetime League Points decide your rank. Each rank you reach grants a permanent mark bonus that stacks as you climb — reaching a higher rank keeps every bonus below it.

Rank League Points Mark bonus Apprentice Provisioner — — Journeyman Provisioner 750 +250 Expert Provisioner 2,500 +750 Master Provisioner 7,500 +2,000 Legendary Provisioner 20,000 +5,000

Last updated: 2026-06-14 13:15 UTC

docs.title: Seasonal Events
docs.text:
From time to time — around holidays and special occasions — the server runs a seasonal event that boosts the marks you earn from Hunting League kills. During an event window, every qualifying kill pays a mark multiplier on top of your usual amount, for a limited time.

Summary

During a seasonal event, Hunting League kills earn bonus marks (a mark multiplier) for a limited time. Check below to see whether one is running.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
When an event is live, the bonus is fully automatic — just keep hunting. Each event has:

  • A name that appears in the kill bonus message so you know it's active.
  • A mark multiplier (for example, 2× for double marks or 1.5× for a 50% bonus) applied on top of any Hunter's Guild amplifier you've already earned.
  • A start and end time in UTC. The bonus only applies to kills made inside that window.

Only one event bonus applies at a time, so you always get the best multiplier that's currently running.

docs.title: Active & upcoming events
docs.text:
No seasonal event is running right now — check back around holidays!
